subject: general
question: An electric iron having resistance (R) has a power (P) associated with it when current (I) flows through it on applying potential difference (V) across its ends. Which of the following relations is NOT correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**P = V/I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electric Power (P)** is defined as the rate at which electrical energy is consumed or dissipated in an electric circuit. The fundamental formula for power is the product of **potential difference (V)** and **current (I)**, expressed as **P = VI**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• According to **Ohm's Law**, the potential difference across a conductor is directly proportional to the current flowing through it, provided physical conditions remain constant, given by **V = IR**.
 
• By substituting **V = IR** into the power formula (**P = VI**), we get **P = (IR) × I**, which simplifies to **P = I²R**. This relation shows that power is proportional to the square of the current. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Alternatively, by substituting **I = V/R** (from Ohm's Law) into the power formula (**P = VI**), we derive **P = V × (V/R)**, which results in **P = V²/R**. This indicates that power is inversely proportional to resistance for a constant voltage. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The expression **P = V/I** is mathematically and physically incorrect for electric power. In reality, the ratio **V/I** defines the **Electrical Resistance (R)** of the component, not its power. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Units of Measurement:**
 
 
• The **SI unit** of **Electric Power** is the **Watt (W)**. One Watt is the power consumed by a device that carries **1 Ampere** of current when operated at a potential difference of **1 Volt**.
 
• **Electric Current (I)** is measured in **Amperes (A)** using an instrument called an **Ammeter**, which is always connected in series.
 
• **Potential Difference (V)** is measured in **Volts (V)** using a **Voltmeter**, which is always connected in parallel across the points where the potential is to be measured.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Proposed by **Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, it is a fundamental law in physics. It states that the current passing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, provided the **temperature** and other physical factors remain **constant**.
 
 
 
• **Electrical Energy:**
 
 
• Power is the rate of doing work. Therefore, **Electric Energy (E)** is the product of power and time (**E = P × t**).
 
• The **commercial unit** of electrical energy is the **Kilowatt-hour (kWh)**, often referred to as a "unit." **1 kWh** is equal to **3.6 × 10⁶ Joules**.
 
 
 
• **Heating Effect:**
 
 
• The formula **P = I²R** is closely related to **Joule's Law of Heating**, which states that the heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the square of the current, the resistance, and the time for which the current flows (**H = I²Rt**).
